role: bounded-executor author; independent read review of caller and admission changes
scope: Legacy synchronous executor completion only; no native repair authority or durable recovery

classification.note: The callback TimeoutExpired case is a real defect in the first new helper candidate. Renamed-inode refusal was separately specified during implementation and is classified as a new requirement, not a preceding-commit defect. The original 11 mechanisms had no API-absence red run. Overlapping runs below are not added as distinct tests.

draft_snapshot.provenance: Complete 357-line first helper source captured before the two narrow changes; source and snapshot SHA-256 were observed identical before the failing runs.
failing_assertions: Actual READY callback raises TimeoutExpired; observed owned STOP calls were () rather than (True,). The real blocked worker is cleaned by test finally after the failed assertion.

Synthetic unknown prepare holds a directory; renaming the same inode allowed a second prepare call, so calls were [True, True] rather than [True]. This second case is the newly specified scope-identity requirement.
minimal_changes: Only the exact locally-created, fully-closed timeout exception bypasses generic cleanup. Callback TimeoutExpired now follows owned blocked-worker STOP and closure confirmation before HOLD.
Scope-clear and reserve check the bounded table's device/inode witnesses as well as canonical path keys. Existing same-path sticky HOLD behavior is retained.

independent_read_review.conclusion: No remaining blocker identified in the reviewed bounded scope.
checks: Entry HOLD/native gates precede ordinary max-fix/schema returns; READY repeats old and current authority route checks.
Captured routes include idea_lake_db, _project_root, _config_path, and _orze_dir; typed policy enabled check remains is True at READY.
Read-only existing database checks reject declared routes, native attempt history, and unverifiable authority without schema bootstrap.
Incomplete output and stopped return-code-zero results cannot qualify FIX_APPLIED; complete stdout is used for marker and UNFIXABLE checks.
TerminationUnconfirmed propagates through _try and six existing successful-fixer relaunch exception boundaries.
independent_read_review.authorship_limit: The bounded helper itself is author-reviewed here; independent helper review belongs to the other reviewers.

external_baseline_context.seam_note: The original five tests contain an unused future failure.prepare_supervised seam. It is not claimed as the source of supervisor capture or closure proof. Those CPU fixtures authenticate their worker/daemon ownership via SO_PEERCRED and owned pidfds; current new mechanisms inject through bounded_executor.prepare_supervised. No failure-module preparation seam was added.

limits: Legacy synchronous invocation identity only; no native AttemptRef, durable repair journal, restart/adoption authority, or provider-budget guarantee.
Process-local canonical-path and inode HOLD table has a 128-entry bound, no age eviction, and no cross-controller or restart persistence.
Execution deadline begins after GO; preparation/admission callback and STOP/EOF allowances are separate.
At most 65536 tail bytes per stream are retained; truncated or invalid UTF-8 output is diagnostic only.
No primitive implementation, existing test assertion, live provider, GPU training, host process sweep, or holdout access was changed or used by this author.
FIX_APPLIED is textual attestation, not verified patch correctness, filesystem sandboxing, immutable patch publication, or scientific evidence.
